strategy.summary: A compact developer workbench for configuring, previewing, and generating type-safe TypeScript projects.
strategy.colorStrategy: Restrained neutral system with one action color. Accent is reserved for action, selection, focus, and state.
strategy.scene: A developer is evaluating and generating a stack from a browser or terminal while comparing commands, files, options, and docs.

background-light.usage: Default generated-template background and wide app canvas.

card-light.usage: Cards, auth panels, popovers, and primary content surfaces.

primary-light.usage: Primary actions, selected state, focus affordances, and command prompts.

muted-light.usage: Inputs, secondary controls, command surfaces, hover states, and low-emphasis panels.

border-light.usage: Panel boundaries, input borders, separators, and header dividers.

muted-foreground-light.usage: Secondary copy, metadata, hints, and inactive navigation.

background-dark.usage: Dark mode app canvas and code-adjacent surfaces.

card-dark.usage: Dark mode cards, popovers, and primary panels.

primary-dark.usage: Primary actions, selected state, and focus in dark mode.

muted-dark.usage: Dark mode input surfaces, hover states, badges, and low-emphasis panels.

border-dark.usage: Dark mode dividers, panel outlines, and input borders.

destructive.usage: Validation errors, destructive actions, failed generation, and compatibility failures.

display.purpose: Page-level tool headings, shell labels, command titles, and file-like labels.

headline.purpose: Panel headings, form titles, auth headings, and workbench section titles.

body.purpose: Descriptions, helper text, status copy, and generated shell content.

label.purpose: Object names, command labels, section labels, badges, and technical metadata.

radius.strategy: Small product radii by default, with rounded auth controls only where the form pattern benefits from softness.

spacing.strategy: Compact product spacing with clear grouping. Avoid same-size padding everywhere.

elevation.strategy: Flat by default. Use tonal layering and borders first, shadows only for overlays, hover states, and focused cards.

rules: Motion conveys state, loading, reveal, collapse, or feedback.
Do not animate layout properties for decoration.
Respect reduced motion.
Default shape is compact and predictable.
Primary color is reserved for the main action.
Focus state must remain visible.
Do not create one-off button styles by editing shared shadcn/Base UI templates.
Keep the header narrow, utility-focused, and close to better-auth-ui's restrained shell.
Search-looking controls must link somewhere real or open a real search experience.
Use familiar navigation, theme controls, repository actions, and auth entry points.
Use a compact centered card, not an oversized marketing panel.
Labels, inputs, and submit actions must feel coherent with the shell.
Only show passkey, OAuth, reset, or provider actions when the generated stack supports them.
Left side controls configuration and command output.
Right side previews files and code.
Use mono labels for object identity.
Treat configuration, compatibility, command output, and preview as the primary content.
Mirror the builder's compact workbench feel.
Use shared UI package components where available.
Keep generated templates polished but easy to replace.
Avoid marketing-heavy heroes, fake metrics, and repetitive icon-card grids.

do: Use neutral primary for action, selection, focus, and command prompts.
Use mono uppercase labels for technical objects.
Layer surfaces with muted backgrounds, borders, and rings.
Keep generated templates attractive but easy to replace.
Keep auth, header, dashboard, and generated home layouts visually coherent.
dont: Do not use glassmorphism as the default visual language.
Do not fork shared shadcn/Base UI components for local style changes.
Do not use colored side stripes wider than 1px.
Do not add fake provider buttons, fake search, or fake settings controls.
